issues.legal_issue: Whether a profit from a single, isolated land transaction outside the taxpayer’s ordinary business is taxable as profit from an adventure in the nature of trade.
material_facts: The taxpayer was an engineer engaged in several business activities, but had no dealings in land apart from this transaction.
He agreed to buy a residential plot from a land-development society and paid an advance toward its price.
The land remained requisitioned, and the taxpayer’s construction business began to decline; he later assigned his rights under the purchase agreement to another buyer for more than he had paid.

The taxpayer said he had intended to build a residence and a workshop on the plot. The Court considered that use plausible and found that the Department had not established that his dominant intention at the time of purchase was to embark on a trading venture.
The Tribunal treated the profit as taxable trade income, relying in part on the taxpayer’s finances and ability to complete the purchase and build on the land.
issues.conclusion: The Department did not prove that the taxpayer’s dominant intention at the time of the agreement was to embark on an adventure in the nature of trade. The appeal was allowed, and the Tribunal’s orders assessing the profit as trade income were set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 2(4) and 10 of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, a single transaction can be an adventure in the nature of trade, but an isolated transaction outside the taxpayer’s ordinary business is not trade merely because it yields a profit or was undertaken in the hope of resale at a gain. The Department bears the burden of establishing that the transaction had the character of a trading venture. No universal test decides the question; the court considers the total impression created by all the facts and circumstances. Commissioners of Inland Revenue v. Reinhold was applied. G. Venkataswami Naidu & Co. v. Commissioner of Income-tax was distinguished on its facts; Jones v. Leeming and Leeming v. Jones were also relied on in considering the distinction between an accretion to capital and trading profit.

rule.if: tax_assessment_appeal and single_isolated_transaction and transaction_outside_ordinary_business and department_failed_to_prove_dominant_trading_intention

predicates.tax_assessment_appeal: A taxpayer appeals an assessment that treats profit from a transaction as income from a trading venture.
predicates.single_isolated_transaction: The taxpayer undertook only one transaction of this kind.
predicates.transaction_outside_ordinary_business: The transaction was not in the line of business the taxpayer ordinarily carried on.
predicates.department_failed_to_prove_dominant_trad: The taxing authority did not establish that the taxpayer’s dominant intention when entering the transaction was to undertake a trading venture.

issues.definition: When a taxpayer challenges a trade-income assessment arising from a single transaction outside the taxpayer’s ordinary business, and the taxing authority has not proved a dominant trading intention, the profit is not assessable as trade income.

issues.legal_issue: Whether deciding if a transaction is an adventure in the nature of trade involves a mixed question of law and fact.
material_facts: The appeal challenged a Tribunal finding that a single land transaction was an adventure in the nature of trade.
The classification required findings about the transaction and the taxpayer’s circumstances, followed by application of the legal meaning of an adventure in the nature of trade.
issues.conclusion: The question whether the transaction was an adventure in the nature of trade was a mixed question of law and fact and was open to examination by the Court.
issues.legal_principle: Determining whether a transaction is an adventure in the nature of trade requires the fact-finding body to find primary evidentiary facts and then apply the legal principles conveyed by that expression in section 2(4) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922. G. Venkataswami Naidu & Co. v. Commissioner of Income-tax was relied on for this approach.

predicates.special_leave_appeal_from_tax_tribunal: A party seeks review of a tax tribunal’s classification of a transaction as an adventure in the nature of trade.
predicates.classification_requires_primary_facts_an: Deciding the classification requires findings about what happened and application of a legal standard to those findings.

issues.definition: When review concerns a tax tribunal’s classification of a transaction and that classification requires both primary factual findings and application of a legal standard, the classification is a mixed question of law and fact.
